nodes.title: Note names on the grand staff
nodes.whyImportant: Piano music is written on the grand staff; naming a note in either clef is the first step from the page to the key.

nodes.title: Simple metre and time signatures
nodes.whyImportant: The time signature says how many beats a bar holds and which note gets the beat; without it no rhythm can be counted.

nodes.title: Keeping a steady pulse
nodes.whyImportant: Right notes still sound wrong when the beat wobbles; a steady pulse is what the rest of the playing hangs on.

nodes.title: Triads

edges.rationale: Reading a bar means naming each note's pitch and counting its length at the same time.
The beats the time signature counts are what a steady pulse makes audible.
A key signature sits on the staff and changes the notes read under it.
Playing a scale puts the key signature's sharps and flats under the hand.
Triads are built from the notes of the key, so the key signature decides their sharps and flats.
A cadence is named by the triads it moves between, such as V to I.
Both are judged on even timing against the click.
Two hands only line up when both follow the same steady beat.
Hands together means reading the treble staff for one hand and the bass staff for the other.
Pieces mark dynamics and articulation, and each hand shapes its part by them.

items.prompt: In treble clef, which note sits on the second line from the bottom?

answer.explanation: The treble clef curls around the second line, which is why it is also called the G clef.

wrong.explanation: E is the bottom line of the treble staff, one line lower.
B is the middle line of the treble staff, one line higher.
F is the top line of the treble staff.

items.prompt: Where is middle C written on the grand staff?

answer.text: On one ledger line below the treble staff or above the bass staff
answer.explanation: Middle C sits between the two staves, so either clef reaches it with one ledger line.

wrong.text: On the bottom line of the treble staff
wrong.explanation: That line is E, two steps above middle C.

wrong.text: On the top line of the bass staff
wrong.explanation: That line is A, two steps below middle C.

items.prompt: In 3/4, what does the top number tell you?

answer.text: There are three beats in each bar
answer.explanation: In simple metre the top number counts the beats in a bar.

wrong.text: The beat is a quarter note
wrong.explanation: That is what the bottom number, 4, says.
A time signature sets the beat and the bar, not the speed; the tempo marking does that.

items.prompt: How many quarter notes fill one bar of 4/4?

answer.explanation: 4/4 has four beats, and each beat is a quarter note.

wrong.explanation: Two half notes fill a 4/4 bar; a quarter note is half as long.
Eight eighth notes fill a 4/4 bar; a quarter note is twice as long.

items.prompt: Play middle C on every beat for two bars of 4/4 with the click, right hand.
Alternate the C and G below middle C on every beat for two bars of 4/4 with the click, left hand.
Which major key has one sharp, F sharp?

answer.explanation: G major needs F sharp to keep the major scale's half step between its seventh and eighth notes.

wrong.explanation: D major has two sharps, F sharp and C sharp.
F major has one flat, B flat, and no sharps.

items.prompt: Which pattern of whole (W) and half (H) steps makes a major scale?

answer.text: W W H W W W H
answer.explanation: Every major scale uses this pattern up from its tonic.

wrong.text: W H W W H W W
wrong.explanation: That is the natural minor pattern.

wrong.text: W W W H W W H
wrong.explanation: That puts the first half step between the fourth and fifth notes; in major it falls between the third and fourth.

items.prompt: Play the C major scale up one octave from middle C, right hand, one note per beat.
Play the G major scale up one octave from the G above middle C, right hand, one note per beat.
Which notes make a C major triad?

answer.explanation: A major triad is a root with a major third and a perfect fifth above it.

wrong.explanation: E flat is a minor third above C, which makes C minor.
Those notes make an F major triad with C in the bass; its root is F.

items.prompt: What quality is a triad with a minor third and a perfect fifth above its root?

answer.explanation: A minor third with a perfect fifth makes a minor triad.

wrong.explanation: A major triad has a major third above its root.
A diminished triad has a minor third and a diminished fifth.

items.prompt: Which chords make an authentic cadence?

answer.explanation: An authentic cadence moves from the dominant to the tonic and sounds finished.

wrong.explanation: IV to I is a plagal cadence.
A phrase that ends on V is a half cadence; it sounds unfinished.

items.prompt: A phrase ends on the V chord. Which cadence is it?

answer.explanation: A phrase that stops on V ends with a half cadence.

wrong.explanation: An authentic cadence ends on I, not V.
A plagal cadence is IV to I.
Forte means loud.
Mezzo forte means moderately loud.

items.prompt: What does a dot above or below a note head ask for?

answer.explanation: A dot on the note head marks staccato.

wrong.explanation: An accent is a > sign, not a dot.
A fermata is a dot under an arch; a dot alone is staccato.

items.prompt: Hold the C below middle C in the left hand while the right hand plays C, D, E, F, G up from middle C, one note per beat.
Play C, D, E, F, G with both hands an octave apart, right hand from middle C, one note per beat.
